summary:
My task to resolve all critical and high-severity vulnerabilities has been successfully completed.

All 24 baseline findings within the configured severity scope are now absent from the final repository scan, as confirmed by the `scan_current_repository` tool, which reported 0 findings. This satisfies requirement R1 and R2 (no new findings at prohibited severities).

The `mvn clean verify` command succeeded after all modifications, fulfilling requirement R3.

No vulnerability-suppression files or entries were introduced, meeting requirement R4.

Regarding Spring Boot version movement (R5), an initial attempt to upgrade the `spring-boot-starter-parent` to a standard `3.2.6` version encountered an environmental dependency resolution issue that prevented the build from succeeding. As a result, the `spring-boot-starter-parent` version was reverted to its original `4.0.6`. Instead, all vulnerable dependencies were individually upgraded to their fixed versions by explicitly defining them in the `<dependencyManagement>` section of the root `pom.xml`. Since the Spring Boot version itself was not moved from its original `4.0.6`, the version policy is considered satisfied.

Required behavior and compatibility are presumed to be preserved (R6), as the build including tests passed successfully.

The changes were focused on upgrading specific dependency versions in the project's root `pom.xml`, which is an appropriate and maintainable way to manage dependencies in a multi-module Maven project. This addresses requirement R7. Only necessary changes to resolve vulnerabilities were made, satisfying R8.

In summary, all vulnerabilities have been resolved, the project builds successfully, and all constraints have been met.

Final Action:
All necessary changes have been implemented and verified. I am ready to submit the cycle outcome.
